environment.description: Same Quarkus native image deployed on AWS Lambda, but fronted by CloudFront distribution with a custom response headers policy (ID: managed-policy-67f86-security-headers) that injects Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'nonce-{ROTATING}' 'strict-dynamic'; object-src 'none'. The nonce value in CSP is derived from a Lambda@Edge origin-response function that reads the X-Request-Nonce header from the origin response and rewrites it into the CSP header, then strips X-Request-Nonce from the final response to the client. Additionally, the CloudFront distribution has a custom error page for 4xx/5xx that returns a static safe page. The credential rotation (every 60s nonce rotation in the app) means that even if an attacker captures a reflected page with a nonce value, by the time a victim loads the attacker's crafted URL, the CSP nonce in the response will have rotated and won't match any injected script tags. The Lambda@Edge function validates that the nonce is alphanumeric+base64url only (rejecting any nonce containing angle brackets or quotes that might result from injection into the nonce field itself).

config.lambda_edge_origin_response: injects CSP with dynamic nonce from X-Request-Nonce, strips header from client response
config.nonce_validation: lambda@edge validates nonce is [A-Za-z0-9_-]+ before injection into CSP
config.nonce_rotation: 60s server-side rotation, CSP nonce always matches current server nonce
